archetypes.name: shell-compat
archetypes.rationale: Bash 3.2 compatibility is a hard repo constraint enforced by lint-bash32; the new with_transient_retry wraps introduce local vars, array expansions, and set -u patterns that each need verification against BASH_AUTHORING.md §3 prohibitions before those forms can be trusted as safe.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect every new code construct proposed by the plan against the Bash 3.2 constraint list in BASH_AUTHORING.md §3: no associative arrays, no namerefs, no mapfile/readarray, no ${var^^} case operators, no &>> redirection. Pay special attention to the array expansion ${GH_REPO_ARGS[@]+"${GH_REPO_ARGS[@]}"} in create-pr.sh, mktemp patterns and local variable declarations under set -uo pipefail or set -euo pipefail, and any _WTR_OUT/_WTR_RC capture forms that might rely on Bash 4+ behavior. Cross-check each proposed construct against existing lib-net.sh callers to confirm the form already in use is Bash 3.2-safe, and flag any new form the plan introduces that has no established precedent in those callers. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: harness-fidelity
archetypes.rationale: The plan reuses count-file flip and PATH-stub patterns from existing harnesses, but the actual stub dispatch in test-create-pr.sh and test-merge-pr.sh must already support splitting gh pr list from gh pr create and intercepting gh pr checks transients for the described cases to work without adding new dispatch branches the plan omits.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read scripts/test-create-pr.sh and scripts/test-merge-pr.sh to map how each PATH-stub gh/git command currently dispatches on subcommand and mode. Verify that the plan's new test cases — GH_MODE or count-file flip for the recovery-list transient in create-pr and view/checks count-file flips in merge-pr — are consistent with the actual dispatch structure already in each stub, or flag where a new dispatch branch would be required that the plan does not mention. Check whether the plan's assertion that the conflict-text URL fallback test is preserved is testable given the current stub shape, and whether the new test for test-rebase-push-no-push-fetch-retry.sh can reuse the existing git-stub plumbing from a sibling harness or needs novel stub infrastructure the plan underspecifies. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: net-sig-coverage
archetypes.rationale: The plan asserts transient_envelope_predicate_none plus is_transient_net_signature is sufficient for git fetch, gh pr list, gh pr view, and gh pr checks, but the actual recognized pattern list in lib-net.sh must cover the real error strings each command emits on transient failure or the wrapper silently becomes a no-retry pass-through.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read scripts/lib-net.sh to extract the full is_transient_net_signature pattern list and the with_transient_retry exhaustion contract, specifically how _WTR_OUT and _WTR_RC are set when all attempts are consumed. For each of the three new call sites — git fetch in rebase-push.sh, gh pr list in create-pr.sh, and gh pr view plus gh pr checks in merge-pr.sh — assess whether the error strings those commands plausibly emit on DNS failure, connection reset, TLS timeout, or 503 rate-limit match at least one pattern in the recognized set, and flag any call site where the emitted text is likely outside that list. Also verify that the plan's empty-on-exhaustion contract for PR_INFO and CHECKS_JSON is consistent with what _WTR_OUT actually holds after exhaustion, since a non-empty exhaustion output would silently feed stale or error text into downstream JSON parsing. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
